clue.text: Crappy smash hit out to convey seasonal message

indicators.note: out here means broken or wrong, so the letters of the three words are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A dire chart-topping record is used to spread festive cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: The standard greeting exchanged at the end of December is a message tied to the season.

clue.text: Big business street must be this for Scot

parts.words: street must be this for Scot
parts.note: street abbreviates to ST and company to CO; ST wrapped round CO spells the clue word Scot

explanation.surface: A Scottish road apparently has to be a large firm, a mock-legal riddle about streets.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as instructions: ST (street) holding CO (company) gives S-CO-T, the word Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that owns controlling shares in other firms is typically a large corporate concern.

clue.text: Was curious about Matthew etc, becoming impressed

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: pried means was nosy or curious
Matthew and the other gospels belong to the New Testament, abbreviated NT

explanation.surface: Someone nosing into the gospels comes away deeply moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressed' looks like 'moved', but it means stamped, as with type on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To print is to press type or a design onto a surface, so printed is impressed.

clue.text: To make a lot of noise over something wanted is a bit sensational?

parts.words: To make a lot of noise
parts.note: to yell is to shout loudly
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
a wish is something desired

explanation.surface: Shouting about a desire hints at a slightly lurid story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' journalism is sensational; the suffix -ish gives 'a bit'.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow press means sensational tabloids, and the suffix -ish softens it to somewhat so.

clue.text: Please explain why residence contains old loo

indicators.note: contains means the first word holds the others inside it

parts.note: a home is a residence
WC, water closet, is a loo

explanation.surface: A puzzled visitor wonders why the house has an antique toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal question form asks for a reason, just as a request for explanation does.

clue.text: Big road heading north — favourite American drive

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means read upwards, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, written here as MI
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A trip up the motorway becomes a favourite American road trip.
explanation.walkthrough: M1 is the London to Leeds motorway; its 1 stands for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the driving force or momentum behind something, so drive as a noun.

clue.text: Brief winter season — victory a boy delivered

indicators.note: delivered means set free, so these pieces are released from the phrase

parts.note: the phrase is the source the pieces come out of; its run of letters ... in the middle is a coincidence, since victory, a and boy must all be used
a win is a victory
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A short winter, and a baby boy is born after a win.
explanation.walkthrough: From WINTERSEASON remove WIN, then A, then SON, leaving TER and SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse and brief are both adjectives for something short and clipped.

clue.text: A new work outside hospital in a mound of earth

indicators.note: outside means this word sits round the next one

parts.note: to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: A fresh piece of art is placed outside the hospital on a mound.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants build a heap of soil over their nest, a small earthen mound.

clue.text: Amsterdam again is seen to be this!

definitions.text: Amsterdam again is seen to be this!

indicators.note: the clue declares that the two words are themselves a shuffled version of the solution

explanation.surface: A visitor returning to the Dutch capital finds it transformed.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of AMSTERDAM AGAIN rearrange into the answer, which is what the clue says they are.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase whose letters are rearranged to form another word has been turned into an anagram.

clue.text: Learners without financial support — it hurts, making one sick

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the learners go round the support

parts.note: L is a learner, as on L-plates, so learners are LL
aid is financial help
ow is the cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: Students without grants are in pain and feel unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone laid low has been knocked down by illness, so is unwell.

clue.text: Joke about educated woman, who didn't recognise Noel?

indicators.note: about means around, so the joke surrounds the woman

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
Rita is the title character of the play Educating Rita

explanation.surface: A quip about a learned woman who snubbed someone named Noel.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel means Christmas; English Puritans banned its celebration in the 1640s.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventeenth-century Protestant zealots suppressed Christmas festivities, refusing to recognise the holiday.

clue.text: Church anthem — it's lacking jazzy element

indicators.note: lacking means missing, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: an introit is the chant sung at the start of Mass
it's gives the letters of it

explanation.surface: A hymn lacks something jazzy.
explanation.definitionFit: A jazz number opens with a short opening passage before the main tune, so it is a part of a jazz piece.

clue.text: About to go flying

definitions.meaning: on the point of departing, ready to leave
in flight, airborne like a bird

explanation.surface: Someone poised to depart by plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in flight, and figuratively in motion or just leaving.

clue.text: Virtue having rows in upper part of theatre

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the rows go within the theatre part

parts.note: the gods is the highest gallery of a theatre
lines are rows

explanation.surface: Good behaviour shown by the seating rows up in the gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'gods' is British slang for a theatre's top gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety, being devout and righteous, is a moral quality or virtue.

clue.text: Musical set left esconced in comfortable seat

indicators.note: ensconced means settled inside, so the letter sits within the seat

parts.note: a sofa is a comfortable seat

explanation.surface: Someone sings a set of music while sitting snugly on a couch.
explanation.definitionFit: The tonic system names the scale notes do, re, mi and so on, a set of syllables used in music.

clue.text: It's a source of power, laments 19 audibly

indicators.note: audibly means the pieces are heard, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: sighs are laments; 19 is a primate; Justin Welby was the Archbishop of Canterbury, the Primate of All England

explanation.surface: A power source mourns the 19 answer, said aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: Sizewell B is a nuclear power station in Suffolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suffolk nuclear reactor generates electricity, so it is a source of power.

clue.text: Edible plant, yellow and long, getting chopped

parts.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry

indicators.note: getting chopped means cut short, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: to ache is to long for

explanation.surface: A yellow vegetable with long leaves is cut up for cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a leafy herb related to spinach, eaten as a vegetable, so a plant fit to eat.

clue.text: Angle presented by extreme characters — I say nothing must be forbidden

parts.note: A and Z are the first and last letters of the alphabet

indicators.note: must be forbidden means banned, so the letter is barred from the word

parts.note: to mouth is to say words
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An outsider declares that nothing can be banned.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearing measured round the horizon from north is an angle used in navigation and astronomy.

clue.text: Drug starts to take effect with little woman admitting state of confusion

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the confusion goes inside
starts to means the first letters of the next two words

parts.note: Pam is a short form of the woman's name Pamela
a maze is a bewildering state

explanation.surface: A sedative kicks in for a small woman, leaving her bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a benzodiazepine medicine prescribed for sleeplessness, so a drug.

clue.text: Name of place in which American uncle stables horse

indicators.note: stables means houses, so the uncle holds the horse

parts.note: Uncle Tom, from Uncle Tom's Cabin, is an American uncle
a pony is a horse

explanation.surface: A place where a relative from the States keeps a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A place name is called a toponym, from the Greek for place and name.

clue.text: Mum sitting on varnish can, losing sight of bottom, stick

indicators.note: sitting on means placed above in a down clue, so it comes first

parts.note: ma is mum
lac is a resin used for varnish

indicators.note: losing sight of bottom means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Mum perched on a tin of varnish loses sight of the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Malacca is a cane walking stick made from rattan.

clue.text: Thomas Becket? Proper troublemaker!

parts.note: prim means proper
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Was the archbishop a stickler or a troublemaker?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Becket as an example: he was Archbishop of Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: Becket was Archbishop of Canterbury, a senior bishop who is a primate by title.

clue.text: Head's essential nature comes through in speech

definitions.note: head's stands for head is; the definition is head

indicators.note: comes through in speech means the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: a principle is a fundamental nature or basis

explanation.surface: A school head's true character shows when giving a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A school head or chief person is called by this title, especially in colleges.

clue.text: Old peasant conveys love for girl in song

indicators.note: conveys means carries, so the peasant holds the love

parts.note: a carl is an old word for a churl or peasant
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: A medieval peasant sings of love for a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is both a girl's name and a festive song.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name that is also a festive song, as in Oh! Carol.

clue.text: Say nothing in card game

definitions.meaning: an old exclamation meaning hush or be silent
a trick-taking card game for four players

explanation.surface: Keep quiet during a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The word was an interjection calling for silence and is also a classic partnership card game.

clue.text: One runt suffering — it's very small

indicators.note: suffering means distressed, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A sickly runt of a litter is tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A subatomic particle in the atomic nucleus is minute.

clue.text: Vehicles covering distance — they may collect bins

indicators.note: covering means wrapped round, so the vehicles go round the distance

parts.note: cars are vehicles
an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: Dustcarts travel some way to pick up rubbish bins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bins' are wine racks, not rubbish bins.
explanation.definitionFit: Underground storerooms hold wine bins, racks where bottles are kept.

clue.text: A mellow beer had to be brewed — yeast essential for making it

indicators.note: brewed means mixed up, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A smooth ale needed brewing, with yeast vital to the process.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeast is needed for beer and for the answer, giving the clue its double sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A loaf of wholegrain bread is leavened, so yeast is vital to making it.
